definitions.series: The Runs that share a benchmark, params, build, instance type and zone ID.
definitions.time_per_repetition: Per Run: for each counted sample (warmup samples left out), sample_ended.t minus sample_started.t, divided by the sample's repetitions; the Run's number is the median of those (the mean of the two middle values when there is an even number of samples).
definitions.bytes_per_second: Per Run, where the benchmark observed bytes_per_repetition: bytes_per_repetition × 10^9 / the Run's time per repetition in nanoseconds.
definitions.percentiles: 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles across the counted Runs of a Series, and of each group, by linear interpolation between closest ranks (R type 7): with n values sorted, h = (n − 1) × p / 100 and the percentile is x[⌊h⌋] + (h − ⌊h⌋) × (x[⌊h⌋+1] − x[⌊h⌋]). Each number's percentiles are taken over that number's values, so the bytes-per-second percentiles are not the time percentiles inverted.
definitions.counted: A Run counts when its binary exited 0, every stdout line is an event that matches the events schema (which the data API serves at v1/schemas/events.schema.json), and the stream obeys every one of these order rules: started first and once (and without quick: true, which marks a developer's trial stream); finished last and once; samples numbered from 0 in order, each starting only when none is open and at a t no earlier than the previous sample's sample_ended; every sample_ended closing the open sample, of the same number, at a t no earlier than its start, and every sample closed; each observed key once; exactly one verified; and as many counted samples as the Run asked for. Any other Run is failed: shown, with the reasons, and in no percentile.
definitions.groups: Within a Series, the Runs whose split facts are all equal make one group. Groups are lettered in the order each first appears, and may interleave in time. A dump section is compared whole, apart from the per-boot values listed as left out; a fact read from such a section is canonical-json-sha256:<hex>, the sha256 of what remains as JSON with keys sorted and no whitespace (lscpu's output is re-written that way too).
definitions.differed: For each pair of consecutive Runs in a Series, every split fact and every dump section of the before-dump whose hash changed, split on or not, with the top-level keys that changed for the sections that are read. Each changed section is marked: it splits, its change lies only in what is left out, or it is not split on.

split_on.what: runner: the manifest of the runner that launched the binary, a blob listing each of its files with its hash
dump section cpuid: the raw cpuid leaves of every CPU, without what is left out
dump section lscpu, without what is left out
dump section sys_cpu: topology, caches, vulnerabilities, microcode, cpufreq, cpuidle
dump section kernel, without what is left out
dump section process: limits, cgroup, allowed CPUs
dump section packages: every installed package and version

left_out.what: the lines of hypervisor leaf 0x40000010, one per CPU
left_out.why: its eax is the TSC frequency in kHz as calibrated for the boot: 2,899,996 (0x002c401c) on the c6i.8xlarge boot of 2026-11-10 23:36 UTC, 2,899,978 (0x002c400a) on the one of 2026-11-11 00:23 UTC; the other 2,208 lines of the two dumps are identical
the kernel's delay-loop calibration at boot, from the same TSC frequency: 5799.99 and 5799.95 on those two boots
it holds the host name, which comes from the private address and is new on every launch

not_split_on.what: they change with every commit, whether or not the benchmark did
changes on every read (each CPU's current MHz)
changes on every read (meminfo, loadavg, uptime, pressure)
changes on every read (each block device's I/O counters, /sys/block/*/stat)
changes on every read (each Amazon NVMe disk's I/O counters and latency histograms, nvme amzn stats)
changes on every read (the default route's interface's own statistics, ethtool -S, with ENA's allowance-exceeded counters; /proc/net/dev, /proc/net/snmp, /proc/net/netstat)
the routes, MTUs, TCP and socket settings, resolver files and network driver; added for the Service benchmarks after version 1's facts were chosen, and left to the Method that reads their requests
holds the root volume's serial, which is new on every launch
holds the instance ID, private address and launch time, new on every launch; its instance type and zone ID make the Series, and its image is split on
the box script's record of preparing the disks at boot: every command with its start and end times, new on every boot, and what it printed, which names the disks by serial

the EC2 API's catalog record of the instance type, taken once per boot: the instance type already makes the Series, AWS may revise the record without the machine changing, and a failed call records its error instead
names the instance's volumes and holds their creation times and status, new on every launch
names the instance and holds its addresses and launch time, new on every launch
the EC2 API's record of the path out of the box's subnet, taken once per boot: the route tables and the VPC's endpoints, shared by every box of the stage; a failed call records its error instead

points.failure: killed by signal 9; the runner was told to stop by signal 15; line 12: the last event must be "finished", got "sample_ended"; no "verified" event; no counted sample (warmup false); expected 10 counted samples, found 0

killed by signal 9 (the runner's 1 s timeout); line 8: the last event must be "finished", got "sample_ended"; no "verified" event; no counted sample (warmup false); expected 10 counted samples, found 0
exit code 2; line 1: the last event must be "finished", got "started"; no "verified" event; no counted sample (warmup false); expected 10 counted samples, found 0
